reference.text: We recommend liberalized ICU family presence policies as the default practice in ICUs.
We suggest offering the option of families being present on rounds in the ICU.
We suggest offering family participation in bedside care.

We suggest offering family presence during resuscitation, with an assigned staff member to support the family. There are not sufficient data for a statement regarding family presence during invasive b
We suggest providing educational programs for families of ICU patients to orient them to the ICU environment, ICU team, and ICU concepts.
We make no suggestion for or against specific tools relevant to family-centered ICU care designed for clinical teams.
We suggest providing ICU diaries for families of ICU patients.
We make no suggestion for or against any specific decision-making support tools for families of ICU patients.
We suggest providing bereavement support to families of patients who have died in the ICU.
We suggest identifying and supporting the mental health and psychological needs of families of ICU patients.
We suggest identifying and supporting the spiritual needs of families of ICU patients.
Best practice statement. We recommend ICUs use family support zones or incorporate supportive features to meet family needs during patients ICU stays.
Best practice statement. We recommend that ICUs implement practices to systematically identify and reduce barriers so as to promote equitable critical care delivery for patients families.
We suggest using standardized approaches for interdisciplinary family conferences and facilitation of communication in ICUs.
We suggest ICUs provide communication skills training to clinicians, if local resources permit.
We suggest critical care trainees participate in high fidelity (e.g., standardized actor) simulation communication education training programs.
We suggest structured programs to support clinicians in promoting the delivery of family-centered ICU care.

notes: Reference = Table 1 (p4-5) + boxed body statements: 17 statements (abstract confirms 1 strong, 14 conditional, 2 BPS). Table text clean. R6/R8 'We make no suggestion for or against ...' are printed as conditional recommendation, low certainty; counted graded (per abstract's 14 conditional) with direction 'neither'. Extractor labeled them 'Conditional Against' -> strength_ok=false (direction invented). If direction were ignored for these, strength_ok would be 15/15. Restatement FPs: extractor emitted both table and body copies of 7 recs without dedup. Both BPS extracted as graded strong (raw_certainty 'Best practice statement', certainty empty).
